title: Unified attachments, private previews and recoverable uploads

cases.title: Recheck access after storage read
preconditions: The actor is signed in with current project write access unless this case explicitly changes that access.
steps: Lose access while private bytes are being loaded.
expected: Post-I/O authorization prevents returning protected bytes.
notes: The native Playwright scenario uses the normal Download action and a Linux write lease on only its freshly uploaded, isolated local text object. The kernel's SIGIO proves the real Go storage open is waiting; actual project membership is removed before releasing the lease. The actual typed 404 response contains no protected bytes, no browser download occurs, and the UI shows the denial. The lease fixture does not modify stored bytes or metadata. Finally cleanup restores membership and verifies the original content through the service.

This verifies the real local object-store post-I/O authorization boundary without an application test hook. It does not verify Google Cloud Storage provider behavior. Additional deterministic account-revocation and upload interleavings remain supplemental Go service evidence in docs/use-cases/service-evidence.json; those do not substitute for browser surface evidence.

Surface correction: The native resumable uploader first reads the authoritative session after a lost chunk acknowledgement and skips committed offsets. Its ordinary retry does not resend that accepted chunk with its original reference; exact same-reference replay remains a REST/MCP operation boundary and the native resume outcome is preserved separately.

Surface correction: The native resumable uploader reads an already committed session and fetches its existing asset after a lost finalize acknowledgement. It does not resubmit the original finalize request in this reachable flow; exact finalize reference replay remains required on REST/MCP and committed-session native recovery is separately preserved.
